quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter. You may see it on one-way streets, expressway ramps, or roads closed to traffic in that direction.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstate highways, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you be driving?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, enter at or near the same speed as the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns.
No outlet.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that U-turns are not allowed. You often see this sign at intersections with heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: The two-second rule works when driving at:

options.text: Speeds up to 30 mph.
Any speed.
Speeds up to 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any speed.
questions.explanation: The two-second rule applies at any speed on highways with normal speed limits. In bad weather, on interstate highways, or at night, increase your following distance to at least four seconds.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough room to safely pull back in front of that vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming up so you can prepare for traffic or be ready to turn.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough space to safely return to the driving lane. Make sure you have enough room between yourself and the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights of that vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light ahead. If you have not entered the intersection yet, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the light turns red.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly. If you have not entered yet, stop.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find a different route.
Drive to the next exit, leave the freeway, and go back to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on the road or shoulder. Other drivers will not expect this and it causes accidents. Instead, drive to the next exit.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. What should you do on a slippery road?

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire grip while driving uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly and avoid quick turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel to the left.
Turn the steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: During a skid, turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is skidding. Take your foot off the gas and do not use the brakes. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What speed should you always drive?

options.text: The speed of other vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never exceed the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: On a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Another driver is passing you in a no passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps both drivers avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: What does the Implied Consent Law mean?

options.text: You will take a test if asked to check the alcohol or drug level in your blood.
Traffic laws apply at an intersection even without signs or signals.
You do not have to take a test if asked to check the alcohol or drug level in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will take a test if asked to check the alcohol or drug level in your blood.
questions.explanation: By driving a vehicle, you agree to be tested for drugs or alcohol if asked by police.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway through the exit lane.
As you get close to the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: When leaving an interstate, keep your speed until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before you turn?

options.text: At least 50 feet.
As soon as you decide to turn.
At least 100 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 50 feet.
questions.explanation: You must turn on your signal at least 50 feet before you turn.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Only look at the car directly in front of you.
Scan the road ahead to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the road ahead to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Staring only at the road right in front of you is dangerous. Scan the road and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:

options.text: Slowing down.
Moving to a different lane.
Keeping your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If you can, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road curves or becomes narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves or becomes narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is about to curve or get narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all other vehicles have left before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Vehicles then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can complete the turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must always stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need to swing wider to complete a right turn because of this difference.

questions.question: You park facing uphill on a street with a curb. Set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic from another road is merging. Give them space to join safely.
Traffic from another road is merging. Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic from another road is merging. Give them space to join safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging into your lane. Check your mirrors and side, then move to another lane if possible. This gives merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: Large trucks are most likely to slow down when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving through long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on inclines.
